slides.title: Translate for customers. **Skip the robot tone.**
Word-for-word translation can sound **stiff**, or even rude.

cards.title: Natural translation
cards.text: Translate this message into [LANGUAGE AND COUNTRY] for a customer. Keep it as friendly and informal as the original. Write what a local small business would say, not word-for-word. Then translate your version back into English so I can check it. Message: [PASTE MESSAGE]

messages.text: Spanish for Mexico. "Hi Ana! Your appointment is confirmed for Friday at 3. If anything changes, just text us, no stress. See you soon!"

¡Hola, Ana! Tu cita está confirmada para el viernes a las 3. Si cambia algo, mándanos un mensaje, sin problema. ¡Nos vemos pronto!

**Back to English:** Hi, Ana! Your appointment is confirmed for Friday at 3. If anything changes, send us a message, no problem. See you soon!

caption:
How to translate customer messages with AI so they sound natural

Word-for-word translation is how a friendly text turns stiff. Ask for what a local business would actually say, then check it.

Copy this:

"Translate this message into [LANGUAGE AND COUNTRY] for a customer. Keep it as friendly and informal as the original. Write what a local small business would say, not word-for-word. Then translate your version back into English so I can check it. Message: [PASTE MESSAGE]"

I tried it with an invented hair salon's appointment text in Spanish for Mexico. The back-translation matched the original, so you can check the meaning without speaking Spanish.

Two tips: name the country, not just the language. And for anything legal, medical or about money, have a fluent person check it.
